newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: HOCKEY-GERMANY BEAT NETHERLANDS IN JUBILEE FINAL.
newsitem.headline: HOCKEY-GERMANY BEAT NETHERLANDS IN JUBILEE FINAL.

text.p: Germany beat Olympic champions the Netherlands for the second day in a row when they won the final of the Golden Jubilee of Pakistan men's hockey tournament 3-1 on Sunday.
It was a repeat of the score between the two teams in Saturday's final round robin game which had ended a 25-match unbeaten run for the Dutch.
The Netherlands took the lead when young German goalkeeper Nils Kowalczek saved a fierce shot by Marten Eikelboom in the 18th minute but could not prevent the ball spinning over the line.
But it took Germany only four minutes to equalise through Peter Streich.

Gemany went ahead in the 49th minute when Bjorn Michel scored with a flick shot at their fourth penalty corner. Then, as the Dutch searched frantically for an equaliser, the Germans counter-attacked five minutes from time and Oliver Domke settled the game.
German coach Paul Lissek was delighted with the result but acknowledged that the Dutch were missing two key players in captain Stephan Veen and Erik Jazet.
"We have to be realistic," he said. "This was not the full Dutch team but it's good that my young team beat such a confident side twice. It's a good start for raising a team for the World Cup."

Pakistan may have failed to make the final of the special tournament to mark hockey's contribution to their first 50 years, but they celebrated Pakistan Day by beating Australia, the Olympic bronze medallists, 7-4 in the bronze medal match.
